title: FINRA short-interest zero-vs-missing semantics re-audit

prior_phase37_reclassification.previous_claim: 98 of 335 symbols represented approximately 29% short-interest coverage
prior_phase37_reclassification.corrected_interpretation: 98 unique symbols with positive reported-position rows in the Phase 31 artifact; this is not automatically a missing-data rate
basis: FINRA Regulatory Notice 16-32 states firms need not report zero positions for issue symbols with no current-cycle short position
FINRA consolidated short-interest dataset is an aggregate of reported positions across exchange-listed and OTC equities
A complete snapshot plus effective-dated eligible security and no row may support a structural zero; failed snapshots and unresolved identities remain unknown

phase31_observed_artifact.note: Counts describe observed positive-row incidence in the retrieved artifact, not full effective coverage.

source_feasibility.scope: Aggregate reported short positions across exchange-listed and OTC equity securities
source_feasibility.historical_depth: Five years; all-exchange short-interest data from June 2022 per FINRA January 2023 release notes
source_feasibility.availability: Available via FINRA API by 16:40 America/New_York on official publication date

withdrawn_proposal.implication: Do not assume proposed weekly reporting, arranged-financing additions, or deleted-symbol final reports are in force.

required_zero_inference_gates: Complete settlement-date snapshot with reconciled pagination and no transport/API errors
Effective-dated security identity and evidence the security was active/in-scope at settlement
Market/listing scope validated for the date
No row for the effective security key in the complete snapshot
required_missing_states: Security inactive or outside documented source scope
data_quality_controls: Preserve stockSplitFlag and normalize share counts across splits
Do not blindly use changePercent when prior short position is zero or absent
Treat averageDailyVolumeQuantity as excluding non-media trades
Do not interpret FINRA reported short interest as total economic short exposure or institutional identity
